entities.name: USER
entities.rationale: Represents the end users/travelers accessing the Al Musafir travel platform, labeled as USER on the whiteboard.

entities.name: CLOUDFRONT
entities.rationale: Amazon CloudFront CDN serving content and providing the initial entry point for user traffic, labeled CLOUDFRONT.

entities.name: S3
entities.rationale: Amazon S3 storing static content and images cost-effectively, labeled S3.

entities.name: LAMBDA
entities.rationale: AWS Lambda providing edge intelligence to inspect incoming traffic and decide routing by region and device, labeled LAMBDA.

entities.name: LOAD BALANCER
entities.rationale: Elastic Load Balancing routing traffic between frontend/backend and managing traffic distribution between legacy and microservices, labeled LOAD BALANCER.

entities.name: LEGACY
entities.rationale: Legacy monolithic application services running on Amazon EC2 instances, labeled LEGACY.

entities.name: EKS
entities.rationale: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service hosting containerized microservices across backend and frontend, labeled EKS.

entities.name: MONGO / KAFKA
entities.rationale: Self-managed MongoDB and Apache Kafka event-driven streaming components running on EC2 instances, labeled MONGO / KAFKA.

entities.name: RDS
entities.rationale: Amazon Relational Database Service used for relational transactional SQL database workloads, labeled RDS.

entities.name: EC2
entities.rationale: Amazon EC2 instances hosting self-managed monitoring and observability tools such as Prometheus and ELK stack, labeled EC2.

entities.name: CLOUDWATCH
entities.rationale: Amazon CloudWatch monitoring system health, metrics, and pod performance, labeled CLOUDWATCH.

visual_connections.description: User traffic (around 300k requests/minute) directed to Amazon CloudFront.
Static content and media assets fetched from S3 to CloudFront.
Lambda executing at the edge to provide routing decisions for CloudFront.
CloudFront forwards requests to the load balancers.
Load balancer routes traffic destined for legacy monolithic services to EC2.
Load balancer routes traffic to modernized microservices running on EKS.
Legacy systems interact with MongoDB and Kafka.
EKS microservices connect to MongoDB and Kafka event streaming.
EKS microservices connect to Amazon RDS for transactional data.
Curved line connecting the service layer to self-managed monitoring tools running on EC2.
Curved line indicating CloudWatch monitoring of database and backend services.
